There’s something super special here. As another reviewer put it perfectly, it feels like a throwback to the PS3/Xbox 360 era. A space adventure shooter that knows exactly what it is and executes it beautifully.

While I could already list quite a few things I love about the game, I will highlight only 2 in particular. The first being the duo of Hugh and Diana. They are SO good together. The second is the soundtrack. Some really good atmospheric vibes.

Highly recommend.

I don't leave reviews unless the game is absolute trash. I genuinely love this game to pieces. I love every single part about the game, hands down. The art style, being in space on the moon, the fighting, the dialogue, the robots, every single thing. Every weapon is unique, every interaction is unique. I played this for stream and the chat was bawling their eyes out. I def did not bawl my eyes out........ Hands down one of the best games that I have ever played. With such a unique universe and story that it is almost IMPOSSIBLE to find something that is going to give me the same feeling this game did.

If you think you hate kids and you don't want to be a dad like I do, give the game a shot anyway, it was the most adorable thing to have Diana by my side this entire playthrough. 100/10.

The gameplay is a very good mix of shooting and maze puzzling, testing your multitasking skills. But what really shines about this game is the dad sim aspects. The dadding is very nice and wholesome, with not a hint of cruel-to-be-kind bullshit.

Pragmata and Capcom have a trick a beautiful trick with this game. This game spends the majority of its opening time exploring what happens when we as humans project our feelings onto inanimate objects. For Hugh the main character that object is a Pragmata named Diana, The Trick is that for you the player that object is also a Pragmata named Diana. I am a 40 year old man, and I found myself watching this little girl and every little thing she said down to the smallest quirks reminded me of my children when they were her age. This game made my heart ache as I played it because of my projections onto this child, remembering the giggles and the playing my kids and I had. This game is made for men, so it is no wonder it had controversy, you can just ignore every bit of that. It is all silly nonsense. This game is sweet, this game is fun, this game is epic in small portions, and by the end of the story if you haven't shed a tear your dead on the inside.

Gameplay is very good, story is basic until the end, Up until then feelings and philosophy will have to carry you which is perfect for me.

Great game. It's challenging but fair, and I love the hack/attack mechanic, beautiful graphics, and what feels like an optimized engine in today's world (unlike UE5). Honestly, I bought it just because the wokies were hating on it, and I was not disappointed. No weird agendas shoved down your throat, just a charming and fun game that feels like nothing else I've played before. A breath of fresh air, really.

For someone who went into this not knowing what kind of game this would be except for a 3rd person shooter, I was plesently surprised with it and I can't recomend it enough. I don't know how Capcom managed to do this but they made one hell of a game!

Also, the voice acting in this game is superb, the voice actors did such an amazing job!

The idea of actively shooting and hacking at the same time is somewhat daunting at the beginning, however I think they found a good balance. So far the game feels like Dead Space but wholesome. I really enjoy Toyama Nao's performance as Diana. I would have a lot more fun though if this game didn't constantly crash. I am still trying to find the right settings or for an update that will fix the constant crashing issue.

This game has a soul. It tugs at the heart of a father with a daughter in real life. The interactions with Diana brought back many memories of my daughter when she was a child. I found myself spending a great deal of time in the Shelter conversing with her, playing games with her, and just sitting back to watch her explore and play,. as I did with my own daughter. A player would miss out on so much by not doing so. Nicely done Capcom. Oh yeah, and there is gameplay too, lol. The gameplay is smooth and challenging, even more once you get to Insanity Mode. All-in-all, a well polished game and highly enjoyable.
